summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for two weeks of diffuse abdominal pain and bilious vomiting, initially attributed to constipation. Imaging showed no acute abdominal pathology, and symptoms improved with bowel regimen and enemas, supporting opioid-induced constipation as the cause. A urine culture grew E. coli, leading to a three-day course of Bactrim for a mild UTI. Her INR was monitored due to Coumadin interaction. Chronic conditions including HIV, hepatitis B/C, diastolic heart failure, and a healing left tibial fracture were stable. Orthopedics cleared her for 50% weight-bearing. She was discharged home with services, instructed to complete antibiotics, monitor INR, follow up with orthopedics, and maintain bowel regimen.
problems: Asymptomatic human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] infection status
